properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 7:09PM MDT until September 15 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Emery County in central Utah...

* Until 900 PM MDT.

* At 709 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated another thunderstorm
producing heavy rain approaching the warned area. As this storm
crosses the area, an additional 0.5 to 1.0 inches of rain is
expected over portions of the San Rafael Swell, including Muddy
Creek, Ramp, Cistern, Ding, Dang, Bell, Little Wildhorse, Crack and
Chute Canyons. This will result in another flood wave moving
through these drainages.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of slot canyons and
normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
The Chute of Muddy Creek, Little Wildhorse Canyon, Ding and Dang
Canyons, Crack and Chute Canyons, as well as portions of Goblin
Valley State Park.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.areaDesc: Rio Arriba, NM; Santa Fe, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 6:43PM MDT until September 15 at 7:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Frijoles burn scar in...
Southeastern Rio Arriba County in north central New Mexico...
Northeastern Santa Fe County in north central New Mexico...

* Until 745 PM MDT.

* At 643 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
moderate rain over the Frijoles Burn Scar and areas to the west of
the burn scar, including Chimayo and Cundiyo. Between 1 and 1.75
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact the Rio Frijoles,
Rio Medio and Chimayo Creek as well as Camino del Canon, County Road
127 and Camino del Molino. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials. Flooding may also impact
Highway 503 and Cundiyo.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms in and around the
Frijoles Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flooding of areas in and around the Frijoles Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chimayo, Cundiyo, Rio Chiquito, Nambe Pueblo, Nambe Lake and
Cordova.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the Frijoles Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.
